own.notes: For integer quantity q in 1..1000, select the segment with the greatest from <= q, evaluate constant + linear*q + quadratic*q*q, and round to nonnegative integer pence. Segment ranges are 1–62, 63–604 and 605–1000. After inspecting the application, I captured 192 distinct own-context quotes using REA. The model selected after 64 observations exactly predicted all 128 subsequent validation quotes: 100% exact-penny agreement and 100% within both 1% and 5%. All 192 observations match the final predictor. Adjacent observations at 62/63 and 604/605 locate both transitions. The final intercept 10288.99 avoids half-penny ties; it produces the same rounded predictions throughout the integer domain as 10288.98 with half-up rounding. This is a predictor coefficient, not a claim about hidden source parameters. Confidence is high, but 808 quantities remain unobserved, so isolated exceptions or additional narrow regimes cannot be ruled out.

other.notes: This predictor is deliberately identical to own, following the explicitly disclosed shared-rule policy that both contexts use the same pricing function. Use the same quantity-based polynomial evaluation and nearest-penny rounding described for own. No other-context quotes were observed, and the own-context validation results are not presented as direct other-context measurements. Confidence in this transfer rests on the supplied shared-rule guarantee; conditional on that guarantee, the predictor inherits the strong own-context validation and its remaining uncertainty about unsampled quantities. The 10288.99 intercept is the same rounding-stable representation used for own.
